result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_both()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse from selected nodes to all neighbors. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6407-L6444){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_both() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} From the currently selected nodes, moves to all connected neighbors in both directions (both outward and inward edges). The current node selection is replaced with the traversed nodes. Works the same for directed and undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Starting from "B" and traversing both directions reaches both of its neighbors, "A" and "C", regardless of which way their edges point: ::: {#16019b51 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B") graph.add_edge(source="C", target="B") node_b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_b_id]).trav_both() [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['C', 'A'] ``` ::: :::
